chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Abi Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I asked him about a woman who died while in a place where there was no other woman with them besides her. He said: "If there is not among them her husband or a mahram related to her, they should bury her in her clothes and not perform ghusl on her. But if her husband or a relative of hers who is mahram is with them, then he should perform ghusl on her without looking at her 'awrah."

He said: And I asked him about a man who died on a journey among women, with no man with them. He said: "If he has no wife among them, then he should be buried in his clothes and ghusl should not be performed on him. But if he has a wife among them, then she should perform ghusl on him while he is in a shirt, without looking at his 'awrah."

key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a relative within the prohibited degrees of marriage who may handle the deceased in this circumstance
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهَا: her private area that must not be looked at
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهِ: his private area that must not be looked at
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt or garment kept on during ghusl

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man or woman dies while traveling and only members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives rulings for the washing and burial of the deceased when only members of the opposite sex are present. It permits burial without ghusl when no spouse or mahram is available, and allows ghusl by a spouse or mahram with the condition of preserving modesty and not looking at the 'awrah.
